title: How To Find The Three-Faced Puppet In Phantom Blade Zero – Triple Threat Guide
summary:
Are you scouring the Wulin in search of the Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero? This foe might be one of the toughest that you face early in the campaign. If you achieve victory, you're bound to wonder where your quarry went. Our guide discusses everything you need to know about this opponent and the Triple Threat quest. That said, bear in mind that there will be spoilers ahead.

In This Article
  • The Three-Faced Puppet boss battle - Weeping Creek Valley
  • Triple Threat - Learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity
  • Mirrorwood - Winter Wonderland and the Blazing Edge
  • Yucong - The triple-phase boss battle in the Crimson Forest
  • Triple Threat conclusion and reward

The Three-Faced Puppet boss battle - Weeping Creek Valley

Your first encounter against the Three-Faced Puppet takes place in Weeping Creek Valley, less than an hour or so after starting the campaign. As you make your way across the cliffside section, you’ll see a ladder that descends to a ledge with a curious-looking statue. The bell right next to it is called The Lady’s Rift.

Interacting with the statue teleports you to a temple where a boss fight awaits. The Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet in Phantom Blade Zero is a tenacious opponent. She will frequently teleport, emerging from rifts to strike you. You need to time your dodges and parries right to avoid damage.

Since this is fairly early in the game, you don’t need to beat her just yet. You can come back later if you wish once you’ve upgraded your weapons and increased your maximum health.

Note: At the very least, try to defeat the boss in The Lady’s Rift before you enter the Mirage Estate. That’s the location that you go to after visiting all four Serpent Houses, and it’s pretty much the tail-end of the campaign.

The Lady's Rift bell/statue (left) leads to your first encounter with the Three-Faced Puppet (right).

Triple Threat - Learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity

Once you’ve defeated the Three-Faced Puppet, you’ll receive the Triple Threat quest. It tells you that you must learn the Three-Faced Puppet’s identity. You can try to scour the world for clues, including locations like the Mandate Encampment and the Mountain of Imprisonment, as they have portals that lead to the domain of the Three-Eyed Puppet.

However, the place that you should visit is actually the aforementioned Mirage Estate. Explore the sprawling complex and look for the Memory Flowers of the Aberrant Three-Faced Puppet:

  • I. The Wandering Healer - In the Training Grounds after you beat Yuding, the No. 12 Crescent Blade Puppet.
  • II. Frost and Chaos - On an altar in the Mourning Hall where you fight Qiu Feng, the Crimson Boneblade.
  • III. Three Souls as One - At the end of a corridor in Leng Tu’s study. Interact with a device to make the scroll move, which reveals a hidden passageway.

Note: After discovering all three Memory Flowers, you’re told to return to the Mirrorwood Entrance--one of the central bells in the Crimson Forest. Do just that and avoid proceeding to the game’s point of no return.

From left to right: The Memory Flowers. in the Training Grounds, Mourning Hall, and Leng Tu's Study

Mirrorwood - Winter Wonderland and the Blazing Edge

Changes happened in the Crimson Forest when you stepped foot in the Mirage Estate. Parts of the region are now covered in snow, and you should be able to walk across previously frozen rivers and ponds.

As for the Triple Threat quest, your goal is to defeat the Three-Faced Puppet. She’s in the northeastern corner of the zone, where you fought Bai Chilian earlier in the campaign, and you'll need to use the Blazing Edge to take her out.

The Blazing Edge is a special Soul Temper for the Sanguine Reach that requires two components, both of which are found in Meigu Lake:

  • One component is a reward for defeating the Gold-Masked One/Man in Black in the Long Pillar to the east.
  • The other component is dropped by a boss named Zhu Yuan, who’s located in the depths of the Sha-Chi Tower.

Once you have the Soul Temper item, use it to reforge the Sanguine Reach into the Blazing Edge. Make sure to level it up and pick a few accessories that boost fire damage and burn buildup, too. When you’re ready and you have the Blazing Edge equipped, go to where the boss is waiting for you.

Yucong - The triple-phase boss battle in the Crimson Forest

How fitting is it that you’re battling the Three-Faced Puppet, and the encounter itself has three phases. The first is mostly similar to how the Weeping Creek Valley encounter played out. The boss, Yucong (in her Steel Mask form), spins and teleports to strike you.

The second phase is when things get a bit more hectic. She will alternate among her three identities: Steel Mask (stronger attacks), Frost Mask (freeze buildup), and Chaos Mask (flames that deplete both health and sha-chi).

The third phase is when the challenge ramps up considerably. Yucong will split into not one, not two, but three entities, each utilizing their respective specialty. If you’re unprepared, you’re going to get consistently smacked around, frozen, and shadow-scorched. Try to focus on one target at a time 

Face Yucong (left) and shatter the masked one for eternity (right).

Triple Threat conclusion and reward

Defeating the Three-Faced Puppet for good nets you the Freezing Chaos. It’s a one-handed sword that has a unique perk, as it lets you alternate between Yucong's three types of states/damage afflictions.

You also receive the Chaos Iron Fragment II. If you already have the other component, you’ll acquire the Chaos Twin Daggers, the Soul Temper material for the Sanguine Twin.

That does it for our guide on how to complete th Triple Threat quest. If you’re still on the lookout for other goodies at this stage of the campaign, then we encourage you to collect all Soul Temper items.

title: Where To Find All Serpent Houses In Phantom Blade Zero
summary:
Are you looking for the Serpent Houses in Phantom Blade Zero? It’s imperative that you visit these locations while exploring, as doing so allows you to progress to the late-game stages of the campaign. We’ve got all the details for you in this article, but be ready for a few minor spoilers in the sections below.

Pangzhen: Green Serpent House

The Green Serpent House is practically unmissable, since you head there while tackling main quest objectives in Pangzhen. The apprentice, Xie Xaorong, unlocks the medicine upgrade function at bells. He tells you that the ornate snake door is locked, as it’s missing the eyes, tongue, and fang.

This location also nets you the following goodies:

  • Green Serpent Brew (medicine)
  • Serpent Gall: Green (fragment)

Crimson Forest: Red Serpent House

This Phantom Blade Zero Serpent House will likely be the first that you stumble upon in the campaign. It’s due north of the Thieves’ Camp, but you’ll only be able to enter it once you have the Flaming Mane. The Phantom Edge comes from the Lion Dance Grandmaster boss in northwest Pangzhen, so just do the main quest objectives there until you obtain it.

The Flaming Mane is used to burn the brambles in this area. Once you’re inside, pick up the loot, including:

  • Red Serpent Tongue (quest item)
  • Loong Emblem: Yin (quest item)
  • Serpent Rattle: Red (fragment)

Village of Lu: Black Serpent House

Next, use the Flaming Mane to torch the brambles in the Village of Lu and grab the following in the den:

  • Black Serpent Fang (quest item)
  • Loong Emblem: Yang (quest item)
  • Serpent Venom Sac: Black (fragment)
  • Reinforced Bowstring (Soul Temper - Feather Bow)

Meigu Lake: White Serpent House

The Lóng Emblems that you’ve collected are needed for the Serpent House in Phantom Blade Zero. The den is on an island at the eastern part of the lake, and the emblems can unlock the main area. You’ll find the following items there:

  • Treasure Basin (accessory) - Inside the small building to the right.
  • Sha-Chi Amber Fragment (upgrade) - Go to the back of said building.
  • Serpent Slough: White (fragment)
  • Sundering Dual Axes (dual-wield weapon) - Dropped by Heartpiercer, Elite Shadow Warden.
  • White Serpent Eye (quest item)
  • 2x Leng Tu’s Memory Flowers

Note: The four fragments that you’ve collected are automatically combined to create the Serpent’s Memory, a Soul Temper material for the White Serpent & Crimson Viper.

The Serpent Door and the Mirage Estate - Point of no return

You can place the three quest items--Red Serpent Tongue, Black Serpent Fang, and White Serpent Eye--in the ornate door in Pangzhen’s Green Serpent House. Doing so opens a hidden passageway that leads to the Mirage Estate.

To be clear, this is a point of no return. When you go through the passageway, you’ll receive a warning telling you that you still have “unfinished business.” If you proceed further, you’ll arrive at the Mirage Estate, though it’s possible that several quests will also fail abruptly. That’s why it’s important to tackle key objectives before you proceed.

In any case, that does it for our guide on where to find all Serpent Houses in Phantom Blade Zero. At this stage, we encourage you to thoroughly explore other regions. You can gather more main weapons and their respective Soul Temper materials.

title: Don’t Miss This Great New Action Game Inspired By From Software’s Earliest Series
summary:
Amid the countless games flooding Steam at all times, a new release this week is not to be missed: Queen's Domain. The action-adventure game from Freshly Baked Games takes more than a little inspiration from the earliest titles made by From Software, the King's Field series, but it manages to stand out from other modern fantasy games.

That's the takeaway from senior producer Jean-Luc Seipke, who goes into their impressions of the game in the video below. Jean-Luc is not a King's Field player but very much enjoyed the opening 10 hours of the game--an amount that somehow only equates to about 5% completion, according to an in-game counter.

The gorgeous retro visuals evoke a game released somewhere right between the PlayStation 1 and 2 eras, and is light on story overall, although it leans into environmental storytelling in a way that feels very true to the style of From Software.

Jean-Luc notes the gameplay may not properly sell why the game is such a joy to play. The combat is decidedly slower-paced than many other games, even requiring you to be at full stamina in order to deal damage. There's also no block or parry, instead requiring you to physically move out of the way of an attack to avoid damage. This results in a very deliberate style of combat, where you have to really pay attention to animations and be calculating with your every move. 

What interests me most from Jean-Luc's rundown is the exploration. You eventually unlock a weapon, the Holy Sword Endu, which provides you with the ability to dash forward or backward in mid-air and can be upgraded to provide additional charges. What initially might feel like a linear world becomes something far more dense and interesting as you recognize the way the sword progressively lets you reach more and more areas as you poke and prod at its environments to see where it can take you.

You should be aware that it can be easy to lose progress, as there are no checkpoints or auto-saves. Die, and you're sent back to your last manual save. (If that's off-putting to you and are looking for something vaguely soulslike-adjacent, the newly released Phantom Blade Zero might be what you're looking for.)

Jean-Luc recommends Queen's Domain, and you can hear more about why (and see some very upsetting-looking bipedal fishmen while you're at it) in the video above. Queen's Domain hits Steam tomorrow, October 30, for $20 and is deemed Verified on both Steam Machine and Deck. A demo is available now.

title: Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
summary:
Beloved actor Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The veteran of stage and screen was best known for his many years as Star Trek's Jean-Luc Picard and X-Men's Charles Xavier, though he also had notable roles in video games, including The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow.

"We announce with grew sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dimentia" a statement on his official Instagram reads. "He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace."

Stewart's role as Picard made him a household name, and following the conclusion of Star Trek: The Next Generation, he reprised the role in several Star Trek films as well as the series Star Trek: Picard.

Though best known for his live-action roles like Picard and Xavier, Stewart was also known for his iconic voice. Alongside the aforementioned games like Oblivion and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow (and its sequel), Stewart had voice roles in everything from American Dad to The Prince of Egypt. He also narrated the Ted movies, with his friend Ian McKellen taking over the role for the recent Ted series on Peacock.

title: WoW: Forever Won’t Have Dead Servers
summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever will avoid repeating WoW Classic's mistakes and will have tools to prevent "dead" or "unsustainable" server rulesets, Blizzard said.

In the past, various WoW Classic servers became "dead" over time, as players either stopped playing or transferred to other servers. Those massive drops in population had major ramifications for players left on the server being unable to find groups for raids or dungeons, as well as for the server's economy and auction house. In some extreme cases, Blizzard gave away free character transfers so players could leave their "dead" servers behind.

While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term. 

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen. 

"If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said.

Greenfield said it's not something Blizzard will jump to unless absolutely necessary and that it's committed to its current separate-ruleset path. Blizzard debated the idea of rulesets during Forever's development and discussed letting players from different rulesets group together for instanced content or combining auction houses.

However, it landed on wanting to maintain distinct communities, in part because of the differences in server economies when it comes to PvE and PvP rulesets, with Greenfield using an example of how it's easier to farm for gold and items on a PvE server. That in turn opened up debates on whether these cross-ruleset players would be able to trade items with one another and the need for other restrictions.

"Ultimately, these are different mindsets, these are different rulesets," Greenfield said the team decided. "Let's keep them separate for now. That is a part of original WoW that we don't want to just throw out completely. But I think the tech is set up in such a way that if we ever did really feel like we needed to make a change, we could do so."

He said those options are merely "levers we can pull if we need to" and that it's important for Blizzard to "stay flexible." That's good news, and will likely give players worried about choosing the wrong ruleset some relief. 

Blizzard is keeping busy in the handful of days left before Forever's launch. It previously detailed how it's making improvements to Forever's divisive layering system in time for release, and announced major changes to racial abilities. 

In a first for WoW, Forever will be fully playable on a controller. WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale recently said Forever's controller support is a step towards WoW being playable "wherever you want" and "on whatever you want."

WoW: Forever arrives November 4. If you want to be ready for launch day, you can technically make up to three WoW: Forever characters right now.

Those massive drops in population had major ramifications for players left on the server being unable to find groups for raids or dungeons, as well as for the server's economy and auction house. In some extreme cases, Blizzard gave away free character transfers so players could leave their "dead" servers behind.

While Forever is going a different route with what are essentially mega servers tailored around specific rulesets, some players might still have anxiety when it comes to picking a ruleset that will be a healthy place to play long-term. 

In the latest episode of the WoW: Forever podcast, Blizzard said it has tools it can use if a ruleset's population becomes "unsustainable." Senior game designer Josh Greenfield gave the example of Forever's separate RP and (newly added) RP-PvP server rulesets. He said there were initially concerns about splitting up the RP community, fearing that one or both of the rulesets wouldn't be able to stand the test of time. He said Blizzard now believes "it will be fine," but does have options should the worst happen. 

"If someday down the line, if something happens and one or both of those populations can't quite sustain themselves, we have options if we do need to say link up their auction houses or allow them to group for instanced content," Greenfield said.

Greenfield said it's not something Blizzard will jump to unless absolutely necessary and that it's committed to its current separate-ruleset path. Blizzard debated the idea of rulesets during Forever's development and discussed letting players from different rulesets group together for instanced content or combining auction houses.

However, it landed on wanting to maintain distinct communities, in part because of the differences in server economies when it comes to PvE and PvP rulesets, with Greenfield using an example of how it's easier to farm for gold and items on a PvE server. That in turn opened up debates on whether these cross-ruleset players would be able to trade items with one another and the need for other restrictions.

"Ultimately, these are different mindsets, these are different rulesets," Greenfield said the team decided. "Let's keep them separate for now. That is a part of original WoW that we don't want to just throw out completely. But I think the tech is set up in such a way that if we ever did really feel like we needed to make a change, we could do so."

He said those options are merely "levers we can pull if we need to" and that it's important for Blizzard to "stay flexible." That's good news, and will likely give players worried about choosing the wrong ruleset some relief. 

Blizzard is keeping busy in the handful of days left before Forever's launch. It previously detailed how it's making improvements to Forever's divisive layering system in time for release, and announced major changes to racial abilities. 

In a first for WoW, Forever will be fully playable on a controller. WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale recently said Forever's controller support is a step towards WoW being playable "wherever you want" and "on whatever you want."

WoW: Forever arrives November 4. If you want to be ready for launch day, you can technically make up to three WoW: Forever characters right now.

title: Artist With Music In GTA 6 Had No Idea About Any Of That
summary:
Cliff Richard is among the numerous famous artists who are lending their music to Rockstar's GTA 6, with Richard's classic tune "Devil Woman" appearing in the Netflix Extended Look. Richard, 86, didn't know about any of that, however, or that GTA 6 is a game and not a TV show.

Speaking to The Times (via Dexerto), Richard said of the partnership with Rockstar for GTA 6: "I was told this happened!" He said his nephew's sons told him about it. "They didn't realize I could sing like that," he said.

Richard was eventually made aware of GTA 6, but the singer doesn't know what that is. “The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?” he asked.

"Devil Woman" was originally released in 1976, so it's now 50 years old. Richard said he's pretty jazzed about the fact that young people will hear his music.

“People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today."

It was reported that Spotify streams of "Devil Woman" surged massively following the Netflix Extended Look in August.

For more on the music of GTA 6, be sure to check out GameSpot's rundown of all the songs in the game. The game's official score by Justice is releasing on December 11, and it will be available to stream and buy on physical media. The same cannot be said for the game itself, which is a digital exclusive. The game will be sold at retailers, but there is no disc: just a code in a box.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the game's file size is gargantuan.

title: Phantom Blade 0’s 66 Days Mode Is Brilliant
summary:
When I start action games, I typically start on harder difficulties, just so I can have the game push my limits and strategies a bit more. So when I first booted up Phantom Blade Zero, I was surprised to find that you do have the option to start on Wayfarer, Pathbreaker, or Hellwalker, aka: easy, medium, or hard, but not 66 Days mode. This initially confused me. Coming to a concession by starting on Hellwalker, I found that you can just switch difficulties whenever you like, which I’m sure can be for better or for worse, depending on who you talk to. 

But after 40 hours beating the game on Hellwalker, I wasn’t sure if the 66 Days mode would be worth replaying the game for. 66 Days mode is the same difficulty as Hellwalker, the hardest difficulty that I had already played, but with the added rule that you are locked into that difficulty and only have 66 lives. If you die 66 times, it's game over--permadeath. You have to start all over. 

Hesitant to go through the game all over again, I hovered over the option for a moment before curiosity got the better of me and I gave it a try. The first thing I noticed is that you get to keep all of your gear, all of your upgrades, all of your builds, but no quest items. This was surprising, as I thought you would start from scratch and work your way up again. But as I kept going, the second thing I noticed changed my impression.

The moment I got hit for the first time, a switch flipped in my brain telling me, “Hey, don't f**k this up." This thought did not occur at all during my initial playthrough, as I would just mindlessly fly through swarms of trash mobs, and if I got sloppy and died, I’d just run back and clean up the rest of the mobs.

This is the moment I understood 66 Days mode. In a sense, your first playthrough is a teacher who teaches you the tools on how to tackle the problems, and learning the history and stories. There’s no worry about asking questions or experimenting to see if something works; there’s no risk and it's okay to be wrong. Just try again. This also ensures you complete Soul’s journey all the way to the end, no matter what, and you learn the truth of the story.

But 66 Days mode is the true test. You have all the knowledge you need of how every encounter works now, and you have your best/favorite builds that you’re familiar with to go through every fight. And you can’t mess up, because you only have 66 chances.

When I died for the first time in 66 Days mode, I truly felt like it was my fault. I fought all these bosses before, I know how they work, I have my favorite build, I have all the tools and knowledge at my disposal. If you die now, there’s nobody to blame but yourself, and I love that.

Being in new situations for the first time and learning new things can be both an invigorating and frustrating experience. At best you understand that it’s part of the learning process, and at worst you just straight up blame the game. But in 66 Days mode, you can only point the finger at yourself given how powerful and knowledgeable you have become, and it felt so much more rewarding to fly through bosses back to back with that power.

This comes back to a general point in game design: restriction, risk, and power, when done just right, are an amazing tool. They can recontextualize the exact same situation in a completely new light, and many other games balance these things to great effect, such as Arc Raiders' loot, Elden Ring's runes, and Blood of Dawnwalker's time limit.

Probably the biggest point of contention at this point is that players don’t want to invest 30-40 hours just to get to the mode they want to play. But I would say this is purpose built this way; every game is designed differently, and this intentional choice for Phantom Blade 0, which didn’t make sense to me before, is now clear.

All that is to say, if you enjoy your first playthrough of Phantom Blade Zero, and you feel competent enough to try another streamlined playthrough skipping all the cutscenes and focusing only on the game’s crown jewel, the glorious combat, give 66 Days mode a try. I sure didn’t regret it.

title: Ubisoft Is Pumping The Brakes On Assassin’s Creed Remakes For Now
summary:
What's next for the Assassin's Creed franchise? Following the successful launch of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced earlier this--which sold very well--you'd imagine that Ubisoft would be looking to fast-track another remake while it continues work on future titles. That's not the case, as Ubisoft dropped a new update on all things Assassin's Creed, including confirmation that it's not currently working on any remakes.

"One thing we want to be transparent about today is that we currently have no other Assassin's Creed remake actively in development," Ubisoft wrote. "Our teams are already focused on the next chapter of Assassin's Creed titles, including projects you haven't heard about yet, featuring new settings and stories."

While you shouldn't expect another Assassin's Creed remake anytime soon, Ubisoft added that it will still keep "exploring opportunities" to bring older titles back. As for future projects, Ubisoft said that it's making "good progress" on its darker Assassin's Creed experience, Codename Hexe. An update on it will arrive in 2027, and Ubisoft added that the team remains focused on delivering a "unique vision" at the heart of this project. The other in-development title, Codename Invictus, is also taking shape behind the scenes. This will be a multiplayer Assassin's Creed game, and Ubisoft says hundreds of players recently got to go hands-on with an early prototype.

"One piece of feedback came through clearly though: Players saw great potential in the foundations but wanted more of the pillars that define Assassin's Creed. The team spent the past months acting on it, and Invictus is now evolving in an exciting direction that better reflects those pillars while staying true to its multiplayer ambitions," Ubisoft wrote.

For current games, Black Flag Resynced players can download one final major update. This adds New Game Plus, Nightmare Mode, new rewards, finishers, trinkets, and additional customization options to the Black Flag remake. Assassin's Creed Valhalla players aren't being left out in the cold either, as New Game Plus is being added to the Viking saga on November 5. A heavily requested feature for this particular Assassin's Creed game, the update will also add an optional progression mode where Gear, Runes, and Masteries all contribute to Eivor's overall power ranking. Players can also earn new gear and a Master Assassin outfit inspired by Naoe's look in Assassin's Creed Shadows; a new Mithril resource is being added, and you can upgrade your gear to a new "Divine" level.

While the news is good for Assassin's Creed fans, it comes amid restructuring at Ubisoft that has led to several canceled games, shut-down studios, and layoffs. Trials developer RedLynx is on the chopping block, while 72 people from Ubisoft Singapore--the studio behind Skull & Bones--were recently laid off.

title: All Friendly Shadow Warden Locations In Phantom Blade Zero – Severed Mindseal Guide
summary:
Are you trying to meet up with the Friendly Shadow Warden in Phantom Blade Zero? This fella can be found in various regions, often at the top of a Sha-Chi Tower. His quest, Severed Mindseal, tasks you with obtaining Primal Stones for him to devour. Our guide discusses everything you need to know about this quest, but be forewarned of a few spoilers.

In This Article
  • Weeping Creek Valley: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location
  • Meigu Lake: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location
  • Crimson Forest: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location
  • What’s at the top of the Crimson Forest Sha-Chi Tower?

Weeping Creek Valley: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location

Your first encounter with the Friendly Shadow Warden in Phantom Blade Zero takes place atop the Sha-Chi Tower in Weeping Creek Valley. The structure itself is impossible to miss, as you need to travel there while tackling the main quest objectives. Here’s the gist:

  1. Proceed through the level normally until you reach the Sha-Chi Tower in the north. Climb to the topmost level and tag the bell, then speak with the Friendly Shadow Warden.
  2. Go up the ladder and look for a glowing item along the opposite side of the structure. It’s actually the Sha-Chi Furnace Inspection Crank.
  3. Head back down to the ground level and use the crank on the furnace. This opens a hatch, revealing a Primal Stone.
  4. Return to the Friendly Shadow Warden and give him the item. He’ll thank you and imply that the two of you will meet again.

Reach the top and talk to the Friendly Shadow Warden (left). Then, obtain the crank (right) and use it to retrieve the Primal Stone.

Meigu Lake: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location

Your second encounter with the Friendly Shadow Warden occurs much later in the campaign once you’re able to travel to Meigu Lake.

  1. The main entrance to the Sha-Chi Tower is accessible via the bridge at the end of the cliffside path. There’s even a Powderkeg enemy that can blow a hole through the rubble, revealing a lift that takes you to an optional boss. Don’t mind it for now.
  2. Now, if you want to obtain the Primal Stone, you have to ride a boat. Go back to the Pangzhen docks and sail the boat over to the northeastern side of the tower. There, you’ll see an opening to the structure’s underbelly.
  3. From the Pangzhen Sha-Chi Tower Dock bell, follow the main passageway while taking out enemies. You’ll eventually see another bell: Pangzhen Sha-Chi Tower Lower Passage.
  4. Keep forging ahead and you’ll reach the outer section. Mantle atop the wooden ledges and you’ll stumble upon the third bell: Pangzhen Sha-Chi Tower Lower Exterior.
  5. At this point, you’re going to see a rickety rope bridge guarded by a couple of Shadow Wardens. Take them out and slide down the metal pipe at the end.
  6. You’ll then notice a tall ladder. After climbing it, you’ll be right in front of the machinery core. The crank is already slotted in, so just turn it to claim the Primal Stone.
  7. From there, walk off the wooden board to go back down to the central area near the main entrance. Just go to the top as per usual and talk to the Friendly Shadow Warden.

Note: As an aside, the aforementioned optional boss in the depths--Zhu Yuan the Searing Blade--drops the Scorching Flames. It’s a Soul Tempering material for your Sanguine Reach, and it’s actually tied to a late-game secret.

From left to right: The Sha-Chi tower lower docks, exterior rope bridge, and machinery core/Primal Stone.

Crimson Forest: Friendly Shadow Warden and Sha-Chi Tower location

The Phantom Blade Zero Friendly Shadow Warden NPC is also in the Crimson Forest Sha-Chi Tower. The area itself is inaccessible by default and you won’t visit it while going through the main quest.

However, a bit later in the game, parts of the Crimson Forest will be blanketed in snow and rivers will have frozen over. We’re unable to confirm how and when this exactly occurs, but we surmise that it’s tied to the world state after progressing the Triple Threat/Three-Eyed Puppet quest.

One more Sha-Chi Tower just in time for winter.

In any case, you’ll find the entrance to the Sha-Chi Tower if you keep going south from the Burial Grounds bell.

title: WoW: Forever Controller Support Is A First Step To Playing The MMO On “Whatever You Want”
summary:
World of Warcraft: Forever will launch with full controller support, a first for the various versions of Blizzard's longrunning PC-exclusive MMORPG. According to Blizzard, the option to play on controller is the "first leg of a journey" to make WoW playable "on whatever you want." 

Speaking to GamesRadar, WoW executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale said Blizzard's goal is to eventually have WoW playable "wherever you want, and, at some point, on whatever you want."

The first step on that road, however, is ensuring controller support works really well. Blizzard is using the launch of Forever on November 4, the latest version of its MMO that reimagines the game's classic world and gameplay with new content and features, as a starting point.

"Looking at where things are going when we hear about Project Helix [the codename for Xbox's next console], et cetera, I think platforms will be a bit more ubiquitous," Longdale said. 

She continued: "I think just doing some of the work we're doing on gamepad [support] is going to give players a lot of flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles."

Having gone hands-on with Forever's controller support during BlizzCon 2026, I can say it works surprisingly well for a game that has been played almost exclusively with mouse and keyboard for 22 years. While modern WoW has added some barebones controller options in recent years, Forever's implementation is far superior, working seamlessly without the need for player-made addons like ConsolePort to make it usable. 

You have a surprisingly number of keybinds available at your fingertips (28, to be exact), making combat and interacting with quest NPCs a breeze. Inventory management and navigating menus is a little more cumbersome, but it does feel like a decent tradeoff for being able to play on a controller or a handheld, like the Xbox ROG Ally X. 

When WoW might be playable on something other than a PC remains to be seen, though Blizzard has made clear that if it were making a console version, it wouldn't exactly be a secret. 

But that doesn't mean WoW on consoles is still years away. Xbox's next console, Project Helix, is rumored to be a hybrid device capable of playing console and PC games, meaning WoW would likely be playable on it. According to a recent report, Project Helix is aiming for a 2028 release, may include a handheld component, and could possibly cost between $1,200 and $1,800 if Microsoft doesn't subsidize it.

In the meantime, Blizzard is plenty busy getting ready for Forever's launch, including reworking racial abilities and making improvements to the game's divisive layering system. If you bought the MMO's new optional playable race, the Skyborne, you can technically make your WoW: Forever character right now ahead of launch day. WoW: Forever launches November 4.

title: Aniimo – How To Unlock The Whisperwake Isles Map
summary:
Aniimo's first major expansion is live with the Season 1 "Departure with the Wind: Part 2" update. This adds a brand-new map called Whisperwake Isles, a massive tropical archipelago location with four regions. Depending on how much Aniimo you've played, you might not be able to access the island right away. In this guide, we'll explain exactly how to unlock Whisperwake Isles in Aniimo.

Whisperwake Isles explained

Aniimo's Whisperwake Isles is an entirely new map to explore. This adds four new regions: Crescent Bay, Rosy Mirelands, Wildwater Gorge, and Cloudreach Falls. These areas offer new main story quests, puzzles, and plenty of exclusive new Aniimo to catch.

If you're a new player, you won't be able to unlock this map right away, as there are a few prerequisites you must meet first.

How to unlock Whisperwake Isles

Access to Whisperwake Isles requires you to meet specific level and story requirements. Level-wise, you'll need to reach player level 55 and receive the Grade I Trailblazer promotion from Dr. Lewis.

For the story requirements, you'll need to first complete the game's existing "Everlasting Echoback Song" Journey questline. This will unlock the season's new story quest called "A Tale of Tide and Song." If you've completed all of the launch missions in Aniimo, then you should automatically get a call from Dr. Lewis to continue the story.

Completing A Tale of Tide and Song will unlock the questline called "A Song from the Sea." You'll need to complete this new quest in order to unlock the first region in Whisperwake Isles. 

This new Aniimo adventure begins in Crescent Bay, and continuing through the Whisperwake Isles missions will eventually lead you to the other three map regions.

How to return to Whisperwake Isles

There's a lot to explore within this new island map, but there's a good chance you'll want to return to the original map or visit your Aniimo Homeland. The in-game map doesn't do a great job of showing you how to get back to Whisperwake Isles, as it only shows the original map of Idyll. You need to pull up your in-game map and scroll down on the Idyll map until the Whisperwake Isles section comes into view. It's located southeast of Idyll. This will allow you to return to any fast travel point you've unlocked on the new map.

For more, check out our guides on how to find "shiny" Aniimo, unlock a free Prismana Aniimo, and complete the Wondrous RV questline.
